items.title: Lemma 13.1.1 (2017: 13.1), closures in $X$ and in $|X|$

book.label: §13.1, Lemma 13.1.1, p. 599 (2017: Lemma 13.1)
book.statement: Let $U(x)$ carry the natural $G_x$-action with $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(x)) \to X$ proper, and $V \subset U(x)$ $G_x$-invariant. Then $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subset U(x)$ if and only if $\mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(|V|) \subset |U(x)|$.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1`: for `N : X.NatNbhd x` with `X.IsProperSubset (closure N.U)` and any $V \subseteq N.U$, $\overline V \subseteq N.U \iff \overline{\pi(V)} \subseteq \pi(N.U)$. `lemma_13_1_1_book` adds the invariance hypothesis.

diff: The $G_x$-invariance of $V$ is not used. (⇒) uses only properness (Proposition 7.1.10); (⇐) uses only the natural action (pigeonhole over the finite $G_x$). "$U(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action" is read as a `NatNbhd`: an open invariant subset of the domain of a natural representation, which need not be connected (Findings, Chapter 13, item 1).

items.title: Definition 13.1.2 (2017: 13.1), good systems of neighbourhoods

book.label: §13.1, Definition 13.1.2, p. 600 (2017: Definition 13.1)
book.statement: A good system of open neighbourhoods is a family $(U(x))_{x \in X}$ with (1) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(x)) \to X$ proper; (2) $U(x)$ carries the natural $G_x$-action; (3) for every connected component $\Sigma$ of $\mathcal U(x,x') = \{\varphi : s\varphi \in U(x),\ t\varphi \in U(x')\}$, $s|_\Sigma$ and $t|_\Sigma$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto open subsets.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.GoodSystem`, with fields `nbhd : ∀ x, X.NatNbhd x` (2), `isProperSubset_closure` (1) and `isDiffeoComponent` (3): for $\varphi \in \mathcal U(x,x')$, the component of $\varphi$ in `morBetween U(x) U(x′)` is an `IsDiffeoComponent` ($s$, $t$ sc-diffeomorphisms onto their images, which are open automatically). For open components (3) is injectivity of $s$ and $t$ (`isDiffeoComponent_iff_injOn`). Witness: every M-polyfold, as a trivial ep-groupoid, has a good system (`nonempty_goodSystem_trivial`).

diff: Condition (2) is read through `NatNbhd` (Findings, Chapter 13, item 1); components are indexed by a point in them.

items.title: Proposition 13.1.3 (2017: 13.1), invariant shrinkings of good systems

book.label: §13.1, Proposition 13.1.3, p. 600 (2017: Proposition 13.1)
book.statement: If $(U(x))$ is a good system and $\tilde U(x) \subset U(x)$ are $G_x$-invariant open neighbourhoods, then $(\tilde U(x))$ is a good system. After the proposition: invariant refinements inside given neighbourhoods exist.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.proposition_13_1_3`: for open $W(x) \ni x$ inside $U(x)$, invariant under the $\Phi_g$ of $U(x)$, there is a good system with $U'(x) = W(x)$ and the same natural representations (`GoodSystem.restrict`). `GoodSystem.exists_refinement_subset`: an invariant refinement inside $U(x) \cap V(x)$ (`NatNbhd.invariantCore`).

diff: Holds as printed with the `NatNbhd` reading; with "natural action on a connected domain", $\tilde U(x)$ could fail to be the domain of a natural representation. (1) and (3) pass to subsets: closed subsets of proper sets are proper, and components of a smaller set lie in components of the larger one.

items.title: Definition 13.1.4 (2017: 13.2), refinements and subordinate good systems

book.label: §13.1, Definition 13.1.4, p. 600 (2017: Definition 13.2)
book.statement: A good system $\mathcal W$ refines $\mathcal U$ if $W(x) \subset U(x)$ for all $x$; $\mathcal U$ is subordinate to an open cover if every $U(x)$ lies in a member of the cover.

lean.statement: `GoodSystem.IsRefinement 𝒲 𝒰 := ∀ x, 𝒲.U x ⊆ 𝒰.U x`; `GoodSystem.IsSubordinate 𝒰 O := ∀ x, ∃ i, 𝒰.U x ⊆ O i`; `isRefinement_restrict`.

items.title: Definition 13.1.5 (2017: 13.3), the natural bi-action

book.label: §13.1, Definition 13.1.5, p. 601 (2017: Definition 13.3)
book.statement: For neighbourhoods $U(x)$, $U(x')$ with their natural actions, the natural bi-action is the map $G_{x'} \times \mathcal U(x,x') \times G_x \to \mathcal U(x,x')$.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.biact N N' g' φ g` $= \Gamma'(g', t\varphi) \circ \varphi \circ \Gamma(g, \Phi_{g^{-1}}(s\varphi))$, with source $\Phi_{g^{-1}}(s\varphi)$ (`src_biact`), target $\Phi'_{g'}(t\varphi)$ (`tgt_biact`), values in $\mathcal U(x,x')$ (`biact_mem`), the action laws (`biact_biact`) and sc-smoothness of each map (`isScSmoothOn_biact`); packaged as a `MulAction` (`biactMulAction`).

diff: The book names the map; the formula is the one used in the book's proofs. Convention: `biact g′ φ g` is the book's $g' * \varphi * g$, with source $g^{-1} * s(\varphi)$.

items.title: Lemma 13.1.6 (2017: 13.2), with the discussion before it

book.label: §13.1, Lemma 13.1.6, p. 602 (2017: Lemma 13.2), and the discussion before it
book.statement: $g' * \Sigma * g^{-1}$ is again a component of $\mathcal U(x,x')$. For a component $\Sigma$: (1) $g' * \Sigma = \Sigma$ implies $g' = 1$; (2) $\Sigma * g = \Sigma$ implies $g = 1$; (3) for components $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2$, $s(\Sigma_1)$ and $s(\Sigma_2)$ are equal or disjoint, and likewise for $t$.

lean.statement: `GoodSystem.image_biact_comp` (components go to components; `image_inv_comp` for inversion; the components partition $\mathcal U(x,x')$). `lemma_13_1_6_one`, `lemma_13_1_6_two` from the pointwise forms `eq_one_of_biact_left_mem`, `eq_one_of_biact_right_mem` (one $\psi \in \Sigma$ with $g' * \psi \in \Sigma$ forces $g' = 1$); `lemma_13_1_6_three_src`, `_tgt` for the components of any two morphisms.

diff: (1) and (2) need only one $\psi \in \Sigma$ with $g' * \psi \in \Sigma$; (3) has no membership hypotheses (for $\varphi \notin \mathcal U(x,x')$ the component is empty).

items.title: Theorem 13.1.7 (2017: 13.1), extension of good partial systems

book.label: §13.1, Theorem 13.1.7, p. 602 (2017: Theorem 13.1)
book.statement: Let $Q$ be an open subset of the objects with $|Q| = |Y|$ and $(U(q))_{q \in Q}$ a good system for the full sub-ep-groupoid on $Q$. Given open $W(y) \ni y$ for $y \notin Q$, there are $U(y) \subset W(y)$ such that $(U(y))_{y \in Y}$ is a good system.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7`: for any $Q$ with $\pi(Q) = |X|$, a family `N : ∀ x, X.NatNbhd x` with `X.IsGoodOn N Q`, and open $W(y) \ni y$, there is a good system with `𝒰.nbhd q = N q` for $q \in Q$ and $U(y) \subseteq W(y)$ for $y \notin Q$. `IsGoodOn N Q`: $U(q) \subseteq Q$, $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(q)) \to X$ proper, and (3) on $\mathcal U(q,q')$. Witness: `GoodSystem.isGoodOn`.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: properness of the given $U(q)$ in $X$ (`IsGoodOn`); the book's good system for the sub-ep-groupoid on $Q$ gives properness in $Q$. That $Q$-properness implies $X$-properness when $|Q| = |X|$ is presumably true and not formalized (gap G.141); witness `GoodSystem.isGoodOn`.

Otherwise stronger: $Q$ need not be open, and the given $U(q)$ are kept unchanged. The natural action and $\mathcal U(q,q')$ are the same in $Q$ and in $X$. The proof does not use the book's smallness condition on the closures; it uses transports carrying $U(y)$ into $U(q_y)$.

items.title: Theorem 13.1.8 (2017: 13.2), existence of good systems

book.label: §13.1, Theorem 13.1.8, p. 604 (2017: Theorem 13.2)
book.statement: If $X$ has paracompact orbit space and $W(x) \ni x$ are open, there is a good system with $U(x) \subset W(x)$ for all $x$.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_8 (hX : X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace) W hW hxW : ∃ 𝒰 : X.GoodSystem, ∀ x, 𝒰.U x ⊆ W x`.

diff: The book's "for all $\in X$" is read as "for all $x \in X$". The proof uses paracompactness of $|X|$ through a precise refinement and the shrinking lemma; metrizability is not used.

items.title: Proposition 13.1.9 (2017: 13.2), with the stabilisers and $D_\Sigma$ before it

book.label: §13.1, Proposition 13.1.9, p. 607 (2017: Proposition 13.2), and the discussion before it, p. 606
book.statement: For a component $\Sigma \subset \mathcal U(x,x')$ with stabilisers $G_{x,\Sigma}$, $G_{x',\Sigma}$ and the sc-diffeomorphism $D_\Sigma = t \circ (s|_\Sigma)^{-1}$, there is a unique group isomorphism $g \mapsto g'(g)$, $G_{x,\Sigma} \to G_{x',\Sigma}$, with $(s|_\Sigma)^{-1}(g * z) = g'(g) * (s|_\Sigma)^{-1}(z) * g^{-1}$.

lean.statement: `GoodSystem.stabSrc`, `stabTgt` (subgroups), `GoodSystem.D` with `isScDiffeoOn_D`. `GoodSystem.proposition_13_1_9 (hφ : φ ∈ 𝒰.mor x x′)`: `f : stabSrc ≃* stabTgt` with $\mathrm{srcInv}(\Phi_g z) = \mathrm{biact}(f g)(\mathrm{srcInv}\,z)\,g^{-1}$ on $s(\Sigma)$, and every map with this property equals $f$; `proposition_13_1_9_D`: $\Phi'_{g'(g)} \circ D_\Sigma = D_\Sigma \circ \Phi_g$ on $s(\Sigma)$.

diff: Uniqueness holds among all maps, not only homomorphisms. The proof goes through Lemma 13.1.6 and the bi-action laws, not through smoothness of $\Theta_g$.

items.title: Definition 13.2.2 (2017: 13.5), domain support and support

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.2, p. 608 (2017: Definition 13.5)
book.statement: The domain support and the support of an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$; $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda)(x)$ is finite with weights summing to 1 and equals $\{s_1(x), \dots, s_k(x)\}$ on $U(x_0)$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.domSupp Λ = closure {x | ∃ w, P w = x ∧ w ≠ 0_x ∧ 0 < Λ w}`, `supp`, `suppAt`; the claims: `IsLocalRepOn.suppAt_eq`, `IsScPlusMultisection.finite_suppAt`, `sum_suppAt`, `suppAt_nonempty`, and `domSupp_eq_closure_image` (the first relation after Definition 13.2.3).

diff: At functor level: $\Lambda$ is an `IsScPlusMultisection` (Chapter 11's reading of Definition 13.2.1); the decorated objects $[\Lambda, U, S]$ are gap G.142.

items.title: Definition 13.2.3 (2017: 13.6), the pointwise norm $N(\Lambda)$

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.3, p. 608 (2017: Definition 13.6)
book.statement: $N(\Lambda)(x) = \max N$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda)(x)$; the domain support is $\mathrm{cl}\,P(\mathrm{supp} \setminus 0_W) = \mathrm{cl}\{N(\Lambda) > 0\}$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm N Λ x = sSup (normW N '' suppAt Λ x)`, with the supremum attained (`isGreatest_pointwiseNorm`); both relations for every auxiliary norm (`domSupp_eq_closure_pointwiseNorm`).

diff: The maximum is written as a supremum with an attainment lemma; attainment uses that sc⁺-section values lie in $W_{0,1}$.

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.4, p. 609 (2017: Definition 13.7)
book.statement: $\Lambda$ is trivial on $V$ if $\Lambda(0_x) = 1$ on $V$, and hence $\Lambda(w_x) = 0$ for $w_x \ne 0$. The domain support is the smallest closed set outside which $\Lambda$ is trivial.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.IsTrivialOn Λ V := ∀ x ∈ V, Λ (0_x) = 1`; the "hence" clause is `apply_fiberZero_eq_one_iff` (an iff); the remark is `isLeast_domSupp`.

items.title: Definition 13.2.5 (2017: 13.8), symmetric sc⁺-section structures

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.5, p. 610 (2017: Definition 13.8)
book.statement: A $G_x$-invariant open $U(x)$ with the natural action and $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,U(x)) \to X$ proper, finitely many sc⁺-sections $(s_i)_{i \in I_x}$ on $U(x)$ and a $G_x$-action on $I_x$ with $s_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g,y), s_i(y))$ and $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\#\{i \mid s_i(P w) = w\}$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.SymmetricStructure A Λ x`, with a natural representation `R` ($U = R.U$), the properness property, a finite index type `I` with a `MulAction` of the isotropy group, sections `s`, sc⁺-regularity, equivariance and the representation of $\Lambda$.

diff: "$G_x$-invariant with the natural action" is read as "$U(x)$ is the domain of a natural representation", Chapter 11's reading of Definition 13.2.1, which includes connectedness; properness is the existing `HasPropernessProperty`; weights are in $\mathbb Q_{\ge 0}$.

items.title: Lemma 13.2.6 (2017: 13.3), symmetric structures exist locally

book.label: §13.2, Lemma 13.2.6, p. 610 (2017: Lemma 13.3)
book.statement: Every sc⁺-multisection functor locally admits a symmetric sc⁺-section structure (the proof is the text before Definition 13.2.5).

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_6 (hΛ : IsScPlusMultisection A Λ) (x) : Nonempty (SymmetricStructure A Λ x)`, by the text's construction: shrink a local representation to a natural representation with the properness property, equalise the weights (`IsLocalRepOn.exists_equal_weights`), and transport by $G_x$ (`transportSection`, index set $I \times G_x$).

diff: Before transporting, the sections are extended by 0 off $U$, so that sections are global functions.

items.title: Definition 13.2.9 (2017: 13.11), the sum $\Lambda' \oplus \Lambda''$

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.9, p. 611 (2017: Definition 13.11)
book.statement: (1) The convolution formula for $\Lambda' \oplus \Lambda''$; (2)–(3) the decoration $U'' = U \cap U'$, $I'' = I \times I'$, $s_{(i,i')} = s_i + s'_{i'}$; $\oplus$ is associative and commutative.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.multisectionAdd`, (1) verbatim, is an sc⁺-multisection (`definition_13_2_9`); local form of (3): `multisectionAdd_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn` (sections $s'_i + s''_j$, weights $\sigma'_i\sigma''_j$); `multisectionAdd_comm` (for all functions), `multisectionAdd_assoc` (for sc⁺-multisections); the $n$-fold sum `conv` with `isScPlusMultisection_conv`.

diff: (1) and the closure under $\oplus$ are as printed; (2)–(3) are kept at the level of local representations, not of decorations (gap G.142).

items.title: Definition 13.2.10 (2017: 13.12), scalar multiples $a\Lambda$

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.10, p. 611 (2017: Definition 13.12)
book.statement: $(0\Lambda)(w) = 0$ for $w \ne 0$ and $(0\Lambda)(0) = 1$; $(a\Lambda)(w) = \Lambda(w/a)$; the new sections are $a s_i$; for decorated $\Lambda$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.multisectionSmul a Λ`, exactly these cases; $0\Lambda$ is the zero multisection (`multisectionSmul_zero`); $a\Lambda$ is an sc⁺-multisection (`definition_13_2_10`); local sections $a s_i$ with the same weights (`multisectionSmul_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn`).

diff: As printed at functor level; the decorated form is gap G.142.

items.title: Lemma 13.2.11 (2017: 13.4), $\beta \odot \Lambda$

book.label: §13.2, Lemma 13.2.11, p. 612 (2017: Lemma 13.4)
book.statement: For an sc-smooth functor $\beta : X \to \mathbb R$, $(\beta\Lambda)(w) = (\beta(Pw)\Lambda)(w)$ is a decorated sc⁺-multisection.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_11`, with `hβ : ∀ φ, β (tgt φ) = β (src φ)` and $\beta$ sc-smooth on the object M-polyfold (the book's "sc-smooth functor"): `IsScPlusMultisection A (multisectionSmulFun β Λ)`.

diff: As printed at functor level; the decorated conclusion is gap G.142.

book.label: §13.2, Definition 13.2.12, p. 612 (2017: Definition 13.13)
book.statement: Every $x$ has an open saturated $O(x)$ with only finitely many $j$ having some $w \ne 0$ over $O(x)$ with $\Lambda_j(w) > 0$; $O(x)$ can be chosen so that the index set is stable under smaller saturated $O'$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.IsLocallyFiniteFamily Λ := ∀ x, ∃ O, IsOpen O ∧ IsSaturated O ∧ x ∈ O ∧ (nontrivIdx Λ O).Finite`; the stability remark is `IsLocallyFiniteFamily.exists_stable` (minimising the cardinality), for open saturated $O' \ni x$.

items.title: Lemma 13.2.13 (2017: 13.5), locally finite sums

book.label: §13.2, Lemma 13.2.13, p. 612 (2017: Lemma 13.5)
book.statement: $\oplus_j \Lambda_j$ of a locally finite family is a decorated sc⁺-multisection, with $U(x) = O(x) \cap \bigcap_{j \in J_x} U_j(x)$, $I_x = \prod I^j_x$, $s = \sum_j s^j_{i_j}$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.lfSum Λ w = ∑ᶠ v : J →₀ W_{P w}, if ∑ v = w then ∏ᶠ j, Λ j (v j) else 0`; equal to `conv` for finite $J$ and near $x$ to the finite convolution over $J_x$ (`lfSum_eq_conv_of_mem`); `lemma_13_2_13`: for sc⁺-multisections in a locally finite family, `IsScPlusMultisection A (lfSum Λ)`.

diff: The text does not write out $\oplus$ over infinite $J$; it is read through finitely supported families (indices off $J_x$ contribute the zero vector with weight 1), which agrees with Definition 13.2.9 (1) for finite $J$. The decorated conclusion is gap G.142.

book.label: not in the book (used in §13.1)
book.statement: The text uses local sc-diffeomorphisms injective on open sets and neighbourhoods with the natural action and proper closure.

lean.statement: `MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isScDiffeoOn_invFunOn`: a local sc-diffeomorphism injective on an open $S$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $S \to f(S)$ with inverse `invFunOn`; `exists_natNbhd_isProperSubset`: neighbourhoods with the natural action and proper closure inside any open $W \ni x$; `exists_isOpen_injOn_src_tgt`.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 13.1.7, properness relative to $Q$ versus relative to $X$
notFormalized.label: §13.1, Theorem 13.1.7, p. 602 (2017: Theorem 13.1)
notFormalized.book: The hypothesis is a good system for the full sub-ep-groupoid on the open set $Q$; its properness condition (1) is read inside $Q$.
notFormalized.instead: `EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7` (V13.7) takes `IsGoodOn N Q`, which asks properness of $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(q)) \to X$ in $X$; everything else is as in the book, and $Q$ need not be open. Missing: $Q$-properness implies $X$-properness when $|Q| = |X|$ (first $\mathrm{cl}_X U(q) \subseteq Q$, by extending a morphism from a limit point through the natural representation; then compact sets of targets are moved into $Q$ by finitely many local transports). About 150–250 lines, with a structure for the sub-ep-groupoid on an open set, which does not exist yet.

notFormalized.title: Definitions 13.2.7–13.2.8: decorated sc⁺-multisections, and the decorated forms of Definitions 13.2.9–13.2.10, Lemmas 13.2.11, 13.2.13
notFormalized.label: §13.2, Definitions 13.2.7, 13.2.8, pp. 610–611 (2017: Definitions 13.9, 13.10), and pp. 611–612
notFormalized.book: An sc⁺-multisection with a system of symmetric sc⁺-section structures, equivalence of systems, decorated sc⁺-multisections; their sums, scalar multiples, products with functions and locally finite sums are decorated.
notFormalized.instead: The functor-level algebra is formalized (V13.10–V13.19), with `SymmetricStructure` and its local existence (V13.14), good systems (V13.2–V13.9), and the local-representation forms of the sums (`multisectionAdd_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn`, `multisectionSmul_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn`, `isLocalRepOn_conv`). Missing: the system of symmetric structures over a good system (about 40 lines), the equivalence of systems with the equivariant bijections and the quotient (about 60 lines), and closure of symmetric structures under $\oplus$, $a\cdot$, $\beta\cdot$ and locally finite sums (about 200 lines). Planned for wave 2.

notFormalized.label: §13.2, after Definition 13.2.9, p. 611 (2017: after Definition 13.11)
